brief.user: Nayeli Brandt, a second-year student in the Graphic Design AAS program, taking the Brand Systems course. She's skilled at hand lettering and newer to building full identity systems. Her instructor requires an AI contribution record with every submission.
brief.moment: Nayeli is building an identity for Crumb & Kettle, a real neighborhood bakery that partners with the course. She's drawn the wordmark by hand and picked a palette. Now she's asking the model to apply them across a set of mockups: menu board, pastry bag, window decal, loyalty card and Instagram post templates, with three spacing variations each. prompt:
I need the front end for Studiotrace. A design workspace for a community college graphic-design program, where students can hand parts of a project to an AI model under course rules that record exactly what the model did and what the student made.

Who's using it: Nayeli Brandt, a second-year student in the Graphic Design AAS program, taking the Brand Systems course. She's skilled at hand lettering and newer to building full identity systems. Her instructor requires an AI contribution record with every submission.

What they're doing right now: Nayeli is building an identity for Crumb & Kettle, a real neighborhood bakery that partners with the course. She's drawn the wordmark by hand and picked a palette. Now she's asking the model to apply them across a set of mockups: menu board, pastry bag, window decal, loyalty card and Instagram post templates, with three spacing variations each. Partway through, the model swapped her hand-drawn ampersand for a typeface glyph on two pieces and used a terracotta that isn't in her palette. She has to catch those, send them back with corrections, decide which outputs to keep, edit some herself, and leave a clear trail of who made what before Friday's critique.

What's in the system at this point: Project 'Crumb & Kettle Identity' with a client brief (PDF, 2 pages), Nayeli's wordmark (vector, drawn Oct 28), palette of 5 colors with hex values (#3B2A20, #F4E9D8, #C9A227, #7A8B6F, #FFFFFF), and type pairing (her lettering + Source Serif). Task to the model: 5 mockup types × 3 variations = 15 outputs, 11 of them delivered so far, each with prompt, model version, time, and which source assets it used. Course AI policy from instructor Dana Whitfield: AI may do layout and application but not core marks, and every AI-touched element must be disclosed. A contribution record lists each element as student-made, AI-made, or AI-made and student-edited. Critique is Friday Nov 20, 9:00 a.m.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
